title: OPERA superluminal-neutrino anomaly: timing-chain failure resolved by independent retest
summary: A physical-science anomaly record for OPERA. Encodes the trajectory from extraordinary apparent superluminal timing result to timing-chain fault, independent retesting, and final versioned correction, without treating careful anomaly handling as misconduct.

status_history.note: Seed flagged OPERA superluminal neutrinos as measurement-error/correction case.
Promoted in rev0021 physical-science anomaly/correction lane.

place.scope: CERN-to-Gran-Sasso neutrino time-of-flight measurement and independent retest context

subjects.name: Borexino, ICARUS, LVD, and OPERA timing measurements

claims.claim: CERN’s original OPERA anomaly announcement reported about 15,000 neutrino events, an apparent time-of-flight result around 20 ppm above the speed of light, and explicitly asked for independent measurements and broad scrutiny before interpretation.
what_would_change_status: A primary OPERA/CERN source changes the event count, apparent excess language, or scrutiny/independent-measurement framing.

claims.claim: CERN’s June 2012 update says four experiments measured neutrino time of flight consistent with the speed of light and attributes the original OPERA measurement to a faulty element of the fibre-optic timing system.
what_would_change_status: A later official OPERA/CERN technical correction materially changes the instrument-chain explanation or the independent-retest status.

claims.claim: The final OPERA arXiv version reports a timing result consistent with the speed of light and states that the version replaces all previous versions, making the correction trajectory visible through versioned provenance.
what_would_change_status: A source-level review finds that the arXiv final-version metadata or timing abstract has been misread.
